verdict: ICE's best third quarter ever: busy markets lifted exchange revenue 22%, and total profit rose 15% to $956M.

segments.name: Exchanges
segments.note: Trading in energy, financials, agriculture and equities — shown gross, before the transaction-based expenses in the chart's direct costs; net exchange revenue was $1,542M, up 22%.

segments.name: Fixed Income & Data Services
segments.note: Bond pricing, data and analytics, plus CDS clearing — mostly recurring subscription revenue.

segments.name: Mortgage Technology
segments.note: Software for originating, closing and servicing US mortgages (the Ellie Mae / Black Knight business).

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits across exchanges, data and mortgage technology.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Mostly amortization of intangibles from acquisitions (Black Knight in mortgage technology is the big one).

opex.name: Technology & communication
opex.note: Running the trading, data and mortgage platforms.

opex.name: Acquisition-related costs
opex.note: Transaction and integration costs for acquisitions, including the pending MarketAxess deal.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $222M on ICE's $23.3B of debt, partly offset by $43M of interest income and $11M of other income.
follow100Note: ICE headlines net revenue — the $2,765M left after $865M of transaction-based expenses (SEC Section 31 fees and liquidity payments to traders). This chart starts one step earlier, from $3,630M of gross revenue, so the pass-through costs are visible. Net income attributable to ICE shareholders was $940M, after $16M belonging to non-controlling interests.

takeaways.title: Exchanges had a record quarter
takeaways.text: Exchange net revenue rose 22% to $1,542M — energy up 25%, financials up 37%, ags and metals up 62% — as customers traded and hedged through moving markets.

takeaways.title: Recurring revenue keeps compounding
takeaways.text: Recurring revenues hit a record $1,365M, up 7%, and ICE raised 2026 recurring growth guidance for both exchanges (9%) and fixed income & data (8%).

takeaways.title: Mortgage is still the soft spot
takeaways.text: Mortgage Technology earned just $13M of GAAP operating income — a 2% margin — because of heavy acquisition amortization; on an adjusted basis it earned $219M (40% margin).

oneTimers: Adjusted EPS of $2.02 vs $1.67 GAAP mainly excludes amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and $49M of transaction and integration costs sitting in operating expenses.
Regulators cleared the MarketAxess acquisition early (HSR waiting period terminated Oct 21); ICE now expects it to close in Q1 2027.
